artifacts.summary: Instrumented skill_validate_task_artifacts with caller-visible fix/error/warning globals, gave command-gate-out.sh an always-on console report plus a durable events.jsonl row, added a 19-assertion regression suite proving both acceptance directions, and recorded the --fix-stays-mutating decision durably in code and docs.

completion_data.completion_summary: Propagated validate-artifact.sh's fix/error/warning counts through skill_validate_task_artifacts via four caller-visible globals, added an always-on gate-out console report plus a durable specs/events.jsonl row, wrote a fixture-driven regression suite proving both acceptance directions, deployed, and demonstrated both directions live against the real command-gate-out.sh.

memory_candidates.content: When a bash function's return channel is uppercase globals (skill-base.sh convention), parsing a downstream script's exit-code-discriminated terminal summary line is safest with a per-branch fallback: if the regex for the expected shape at that exit code fails to match, set an explicit error count rather than leaving the accumulator at its initialized zero. A script can share one exit code across multiple message shapes (e.g. validate-artifact.sh's exit 1 covers both a counted '[FAIL] N error(s)' line and an uncounted '[FAIL] File is empty' line) -- the exit code alone does not guarantee the message shape a regex expects.

This repo's no-task-references-in-deliverables hook (validate-no-task-references.sh) matches 'task' + separator + digits (TASK_PATTERN), not the literal metadata field name '**Task**:' (no digits immediately follow the word before punctuation). A test fixture that renames a required '**Task**:' plan/report metadata field to avoid a perceived task-number-citation conflict will break validate-artifact.sh's required-field check instead -- the field name itself never needed an exemption. Reserve task-ref-ok markers for lines that must literally contain 'task N' text (e.g. asserting a script's own emitted message verbatim).
